summary: SurgeQ is a hardware-software co-design framework for superconducting qubits that accelerates two-qubit gate execution by increasing coupling strength (Surge factor $s$ up to 1.8) while mitigating the resulting crosstalk through a crosstalk-free scheduler that eliminates nearest-neighbor ZZ interactions. Evaluated on 127 real-world benchmarks spanning 17 categories on 127-qubit heavy-hex and 225-qubit grid topologies, SurgeQ achieves fidelities up to $10^6$ times higher than baseline Qiskit O3 on large circuits and remains effective even on dense QSIH circuits, where crosstalk-free scheduling introduces $1.61\times$ depth overhead.
motivation: Two-qubit gate errors dominate superconducting qubit performance, but reducing gate time via stronger coupling amplifies crosstalk from stray ZZ interactions between parallel operations on adjacent qubits, creating a fundamental trade-off that prior work addresses only through software-only or frequency-allocation techniques.
method: SurgeQ combines hardware design (tunable couplers with adjustable coupling strengths to realize faster CZ gates with duration $\propto s^{-2}$) with a crosstalk-free scheduler implementing maximum independent set selection to prevent simultaneous gates on adjacent pairs, supplemented by pattern substitution to reduce circuit depth overhead while maintaining fidelity via a digital error model accounting for $T_1^{\mathrm{eff}}=40$ μs, $T_\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}=1.1$ μs, and crosstalk scaling as $E_{1Q}\propto s^4$ and $E_{2Q}\propto s^4$.
result: Optimal Surge factor calibration selects $s=1.7$ for dense QSIH circuits (100 qubits, fidelity ratio $\approx 100$) and $s=1.8$ for real-world applications; compared to XtalkSched and CAMEL baselines, SurgeQ achieves higher fidelity on most of 127 benchmarks with circuit duration reductions and maintains advantage over exponential fidelity decay in large-scale circuits.
